column1: Open-source, free, territory-matched tools for ingesting, storing, transforming, and pipelining ecological + human exergy data for Sri Lanka.

column3: Pull data from REST APIs — CEA, Irrigation Dept, NARA, OpenAQ, GBIF, Movebank, NASA Earthdata
column4: Universal, minimal, runs anywhere. Sri Lankan government portals mostly return JSON or CSV — requests handles both. httpx for async multi-source pulls.

column3: Ingest satellite data: NDVI (Sentinel/Landsat), nighttime lights (VIIRS), soil moisture (SMAP), surface water (JRC), forest cover
column4: Free for research. Covers entire Sri Lanka archive from 1984. Processes in Google's cloud — no local compute needed for satellite layers. Critical for tank cascade landscape monitoring.

column3: Mobile field data collection — community witnessing, tank cascade surveys, soundscape notes, village ritual mapping, estate worker interviews
column4: The citizen science / community co-investigator layer. KoboToolbox is free, offline-capable, multilingual (Sinhala/Tamil support). Matches Anavaratha's ground-up epistemology — data from where costs land.

column3: Low-cost acoustic sensor for soundscape monitoring — deploy in dry zone villages, Sinharaja edge, tank cascade zones
column4: £50 device. Open hardware. Records full audio spectrum. Python libraries for bioacoustic analysis. First step toward filling the most critical LK sensory gap — no soundscape baseline exists.

column3: Access Sri Lanka government open data portal programmatically — census, economic, environmental datasets
column4: data.gov.lk runs on CKAN (open source). Has API. Quality is uneven but improving. Connects to DCS, CEA published datasets.

column3: Local analytical database — store and query multi-source ecological time series, satellite extracts, field survey data
column4: Zero infrastructure. Single file. Processes gigabytes in seconds on a laptop. Perfect for Anavaratha's early phase — no cloud cost, no server, full SQL power. Replaces the need for a server database until the project scales.

column3: Efficient columnar storage for time series — water levels, air quality readings, NDVI pixel values, HIES survey microdata
column4: Open standard. 10-100x smaller than CSV. DuckDB reads Parquet natively. Anavaratha's temporal data architecture fits naturally — one Parquet file per domain per time resolution.

column3: When geospatial data grows — store tank cascade locations, watershed boundaries, protected area polygons, displacement zone shapefiles
column4: Open source. The standard for spatial data. Runs free on any machine. Required when the mapping layer needs to query across geographies — which Anavaratha's geographic axis demands.

column3: Version control for ALL data pipelines, transformation scripts, configuration — also archives the foundation documents
column4: Anavaratha's incompleteness principle demands versioned, living infrastructure. Git IS the institutional memory of the data layer. Free public repos for open collaboration.

column3: Clean, reshape, join, validate data from disparate sources — Sri Lankan government data is often inconsistently formatted
column4: Pandas for familiar flexibility. Polars for speed on larger datasets. Both free. Polars handles the kind of multi-source join Anavaratha needs — merge satellite, survey, and government data by geography and time.

column3: Process spatial data — reproject coordinate systems, clip to Sri Lanka boundaries, rasterize vector layers, zonal statistics over watersheds
column4: Geopandas = pandas for maps. GDAL is the backbone of all open geospatial work. Essential for mapping the geographic axis — extraction/concentration/displacement zones require spatial joins.

column3: Structure and document transformation logic as modular SQL models — build the Anavaratha accounting identity as a chain of transparent transformations
column4: dbt makes transformation logic readable, tested, and auditable. Matches Anavaratha's epistemic honesty — every calculation documented, every assumption visible. Free open-source tier.

column3: Clean messy Sri Lankan government data — inconsistent column names, mixed Sinhala/English, duplicate records, inconsistent date formats
column4: GUI-based cleaning — no code required for initial exploration. Useful when onboarding community partners who aren't Python users. Free, open source, runs locally.

column3: Schedule and monitor automated data pipelines — daily satellite pulls, weekly government data checks, monthly field survey aggregation
column4: Prefect free cloud tier works for Anavaratha's early phase. Airflow is fully open source for self-hosting. Both provide visibility into what data is flowing and what's failing — a form of pipeline negentropy.

column3: Simple automated runs — trigger daily API pulls, run data quality checks, rebuild visualisation outputs on schedule
column4: Free for public repos. No server needed. YAML-based. For Anavaratha's early pipeline, GitHub Actions eliminates the need for any orchestration infrastructure — run Python scripts on a schedule for free.

column3: Define and test data quality expectations — flag when CEA data stops updating, when satellite values are anomalous, when field survey responses are incomplete
column4: Anavaratha's architecture notes say 'a gap in the map is information.' Data quality monitoring IS part of seeing. Free open-source tiers. Connects to the early warning function — if data stops flowing, that's a signal.

column3: Package and describe datasets with metadata — document every Sri Lankan source with provenance, update frequency, known gaps
column4: Matches Anavaratha's epistemology — make the data's limitations visible alongside the data itself. Open standard from Open Knowledge Foundation. Lightweight JSON schemas.
